Formulation
- Predisposing factors:
  - Pre-existing chronic back pain; ongoing treatment with Seroxat (implies prior mental health condition though diagnosis not recorded)
- Precipitating factors:
  - Recent international travel to Vietnam with rural exposure; onset of fever and systemic symptoms ~7 days prior
- Perpetuating factors:
  - Persistent febrile symptoms despite OTC analgesics, ongoing nausea and fatigue impairing work
- Protective factors:
  - Patient promptly sought medical help, agreed to attend clinic, is engaged with health services (physiotherapist) and employed

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute febrile illness following recent travel (possible malaria)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Obtain a diagnosis and receive appropriate treatment; resolve fever/symptoms; return to work when safe
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Perform physical examination, exclude/identify focal infection, and arrange appropriate investigations (including malaria testing)
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attend in-person clinic appointment as agreed (patient stated she can attend central London today)
  - Phone clinic administration number provided in consultation notes to arrange booking
  - Avoid attending work until clinically assessed (patient advised by clinician)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange face-to-face clinic review/examination
  - Request blood tests including thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers (as documented in the consultation notes)
  - Document investigation requests in notes for presentation to A&E or local clinic if patient chooses that option
  - Advise patient not to attend work until assessment and clearance; provide guidance about attending local A&E if unable to access central clinic

Secondary Problem: Fatigue/tiredness affecting work
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve energy levels and functional capacity at work; identify cause of fatigue
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Identify and treat underlying cause of fatigue (infective or other), monitor recovery, support safe return to work
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attend clinic assessment and investigations
  - Rest as needed and follow clinician advice regarding work attendance
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Evaluate cause of fatigue during clinical review and on receipt of test results
  - Provide medical advice regarding work absence and follow-up once cause identified
  - Consider further assessment if fatigue persists after resolution of acute illness (not documented; follow-up dependent on findings)

Tertiary Problem: Chronic back pain; ongoing antidepressant (Seroxat)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Continue current therapies as appropriate and avoid deterioration
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Ensure ongoing management of chronic back pain continues; medication review if clinically indicated
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue current physiotherapy for back pain
  - Inform clinician of all current medications
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Medication record updated (Seroxat recorded; dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - No specific medication changes documented in this consultation

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Need for in-person examination and blood tests to determine cause of fever
  - Specific request for thick and thin blood films (malaria testing) and inflammatory markers
  - Advice not to attend work until issue is sorted; option to attend local A&E if clinic attendance is inconvenient
